mcq.q: How many different samples of size 3 can be drawn from a population of 14 units by simple random sampling without replacement (order of selection ignored)?
mcq.explain: Without replacement and ignoring order, the number of samples is ᴺCₙ = 14C3 = 364. This count matters when listing the sampling distribution of a statistic, because every possible sample must appear once in that list.
mcq.topic: Key terms, sampling distribution and standard error
mcq.fast: Without replacement use ᴺCₙ; with replacement (ordered) use Nⁿ.

mcq.q: How many different samples of size 4 can be drawn from a population of 14 units by simple random sampling with replacement (counting ordered draws)?
mcq.explain: With replacement each of the 4 draws can be any of the 14 units, so there are Nⁿ = 14^4 = 38,416 ordered samples. This count matters when listing the sampling distribution of a statistic, because every possible sample must appear once in that list.
mcq.topic: Key terms, sampling distribution and standard error
mcq.fast: Without replacement use ᴺCₙ; with replacement (ordered) use Nⁿ.

mcq.q: How many different samples of size 4 can be drawn from a population of 7 units by simple random sampling with replacement (counting ordered draws)?
mcq.explain: With replacement each of the 4 draws can be any of the 7 units, so there are Nⁿ = 7^4 = 2,401 ordered samples. This count matters when listing the sampling distribution of a statistic, because every possible sample must appear once in that list.
mcq.topic: Key terms, sampling distribution and standard error
mcq.fast: Without replacement use ᴺCₙ; with replacement (ordered) use Nⁿ.

mcq.q: A population has standard deviation 10. The standard error of the mean of a random sample of size 16 (large population) is:
mcq.explain: SE of the sample mean = σ/√n = 10/√16 = 10/4 = 2.5. Dividing by n instead of √n understates the error. Quadrupling the sample size halves the standard error, which is why larger samples give more reliable estimates.
mcq.topic: Key terms, sampling distribution and standard error
mcq.fast: σ ÷ √n — pick n as a perfect square and divide.

mcq.q: From a population of 323 units with standard deviation 10, a sample of 16 is drawn without replacement. The standard error of the sample mean (with finite population correction) is about:
mcq.explain: SE = (σ/√n) × √[(N − n)/(N − 1)] = (10/√16) × √(307/322) = 2.5 × 0.9764 ≈ 2.441. The correction factor is below 1, so sampling without replacement from a finite population reduces the error.
mcq.topic: Key terms, sampling distribution and standard error
mcq.fast: Compute σ/√n first, then multiply by √((N − n)/(N − 1)).

mcq.explain: SE = (σ/√n) × √[(N − n)/(N − 1)] = (22/√29) × √(292/320) = 4.0853 × 0.9552 ≈ 3.902. The correction factor is below 1, so sampling without replacement from a finite population reduces the error.
mcq.topic: Key terms, sampling distribution and standard error
mcq.fast: Compute σ/√n first, then multiply by √((N − n)/(N − 1)).

mcq.q: In a large town the proportion of households that own a two-wheeler is 0.75. The standard error of this proportion in a random sample of 64 households is about:
mcq.explain: SE(p) = √(PQ/n) with P = 0.75 and Q = 1 − P = 0.25: √(0.75 × 0.25/64) = √0.00293 ≈ 0.0541. Forgetting the square root gives the variance, not the standard error. The SE is largest when P = 0.5.
mcq.topic: Key terms, sampling distribution and standard error
mcq.fast: Multiply P × Q, divide by n, take the square root.

mcq.topic: Key terms, sampling distribution and standard error
mcq.fast: Multiply P × Q, divide by n, take the square root.

mcq.q: A systematic sample of 16 units is to be drawn from a list of 352 units. If the random start is 19, the 8th unit selected is number:
mcq.explain: Sampling interval k = N/n = 352/16 = 22. Units selected: 19, 41, 63, …, i.e. start + (j − 1)k. The 8th unit is 19 + 7 × 22 = 173. Only the first unit is chosen at random; the rest follow automatically.
mcq.topic: Types of sampling
mcq.fast: Interval k = N ÷ n; jth unit = start + (j − 1)k.

mcq.topic: Types of sampling
mcq.fast: Interval k = N ÷ n; jth unit = start + (j − 1)k.

mcq.q: A population has strata of sizes 1,100, 900, 200. With proportional allocation, a total sample of 150 gives how many units from the stratum of size 1,100?
mcq.explain: Proportional allocation: nᵢ = n × Nᵢ/N. Total N = 2,200. So nᵢ = 150 × 1,100/2,200 = 75. Equal allocation (50 each) ignores the different stratum sizes. Bigger strata therefore contribute more units to the sample.
mcq.topic: Types of sampling
mcq.fast: Sample share of a stratum = its share of the population.

mcq.q: A population has strata of sizes 1,000, 2,400, 300, 800. With proportional allocation, a total sample of 150 gives how many units from the stratum of size 2,400?
mcq.explain: Proportional allocation: nᵢ = n × Nᵢ/N. Total N = 4,500. So nᵢ = 150 × 2,400/4,500 = 80. Equal allocation (37 each) ignores the different stratum sizes. Bigger strata therefore contribute more units to the sample.
mcq.topic: Types of sampling
mcq.fast: Sample share of a stratum = its share of the population.

mcq.q: The population standard deviation is 20. What sample size is needed so that the standard error of the mean is 1?
mcq.explain: SE = σ/√n, so √n = σ/SE = 20/1 = 20 and n = 20² = 400. Stopping at √n is the usual slip. Halving the SE needs four times the sample, because the SE falls only with the square root of n.
mcq.topic: Key terms, sampling distribution and standard error
mcq.fast: Required sample size n = (σ ÷ SE) squared.

mcq.q: The population standard deviation is 30. What sample size is needed so that the standard error of the mean is 2?
mcq.explain: SE = σ/√n, so √n = σ/SE = 30/2 = 15 and n = 15² = 225. Stopping at √n is the usual slip. Halving the SE needs four times the sample, because the SE falls only with the square root of n.
mcq.topic: Key terms, sampling distribution and standard error
mcq.fast: Required sample size n = (σ ÷ SE) squared.

mcq.q: All possible samples of size 2 are drawn without replacement from the population {1, 9, 10, 20}. The mean of the sampling distribution of the sample mean is:
mcq.explain: The sample mean is an unbiased estimator: the mean of all possible sample means equals the population mean μ = (1 + 9 + 10 + 20)/4 = 10. There is no need to list all 6 samples.
mcq.topic: Key terms, sampling distribution and standard error
mcq.fast: The mean of all sample means equals the population mean.

mcq.q: All possible samples of size 2 are drawn without replacement from the population {5, 6, 8, 15, 18, 26}. The mean of the sampling distribution of the sample mean is:
mcq.explain: The sample mean is an unbiased estimator: the mean of all possible sample means equals the population mean μ = (5 + 6 + 8 + 15 + 18 + 26)/6 = 13. There is no need to list all 15 samples.
mcq.topic: Key terms, sampling distribution and standard error
mcq.fast: The mean of all sample means equals the population mean.
